candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.25-26 / PDF p.29-30 — practice errors and near misses
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — near-miss reporting / medication safety
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to a near miss by acknowledging and documenting it through the appropriate safety-reporting process even when no client harm occurred.

options.A: Acknowledge and document the near miss according to the organization's safety-reporting process
options.B: Do not report it because no medication reached the client and no injury occurred
options.C: Delete any record of the event so the near miss does not affect unit quality data
options.D: Report it only if the same error later reaches a client and causes harm

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes acknowledging and documenting practice errors and near misses within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. A near miss does not become irrelevant merely because harm was prevented. Therefore A is the best response; suppressing the event or waiting for future harm conflicts with the nurse's safety responsibilities.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The RN is expected to acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses as part of client safety practice.
candidate.source_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.25-26 / PDF p.29-30: acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses; protect clients and health care personnel from hazards
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A nurse discovers that a medication error was intercepted before the medication reached the client. What is the appropriate nursing response to this near miss?
